# Incident Report — Malware Infection, 10.8.15.133 (DESKTOP-H8ALZBV)

**Evidence source:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, ~33 min, 2024-08-15 04:10–04:42 UTC+4). No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present alongside the pcap; findings below are derived entirely from packet analysis with `tshark`.

## 1. Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (confirmed via DHCP request, ARP, and Ethernet source on all traffic from this IP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (DHCP Option 12, NBNS registration) |
| AD domain | **LAFONTAINEBLEU** / `lafontainebleu.org` (NBNS, Kerberos realm) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** (Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ/TGS traffic from 10.8.15.133) |
| Domain controller on segment | 10.8.15.4 (WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) |

Only 10.8.15.133 and the domain controller (10.8.15.4) were observed on this /24; 10.8.15.133 is the only host that contacted the malicious infrastructure below.

## 2. Malware family

**Assessed as Latrodectus loader — behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/YARA alert artifacts were provided with this evidence; this call is based on network and file-artifact behavior observed directly in the pcap):

- The downloaded second-stage payload (SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`) is a PE32+ DLL with a debug path of `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb` and exports `DllRegisterServer`/`DllGetClassObject`/`DllRegisterServerEx` — consistent with regsvr32/COM-based execution.
- Delivery chain (oversized, junk-padded/obfuscated JScript inside a phishing-themed ZIP → hardcoded-IP payload retrieval via BITS → encrypted binary HTTP beacon with a fixed legacy User-Agent) matches the documented Latrodectus TTPs.
- No signature database (Suricata/YARA) was included in the evidence set, so this identification should be treated as **behavioral/pattern-based**, not confirmed by a matching detection rule.

## 3. Infection timeline (all times UTC+4, from pcap)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:10:58 | GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70, Cloudflare) — fake FedEx tracking/invoice page delivers a 2,767,804-byte HTTP response that is actually a **ZIP archive** |
| — | ZIP contains `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (6,990,020 bytes) — a JScript file padded with megabytes of unrelated academic-text "junk" (garbage-inflation to evade sandbox/AV size limits), with the real obfuscated logic (string-built XMLHTTP `responseText` calls, `WScript.Sleep`) interspersed inside comment blocks |
| 04:11:59 | `Microsoft BITS/7.8` HEAD then GET to `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — retrieves the 159,232-byte Latrodectus-consistent DLL over a legitimate-looking BITS job |
| 04:13:00 – 04:42:25 | Recurring HTTP GET/POST beacons (306 requests) to `http://72.5.43.29/` (root path, no domain lookup — hardcoded IP), roughly every 10 seconds, using **User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`**, a long randomized Base64-style `Cookie` value per session, and binary-encrypted POST bodies (e.g., frame 11032, 124-byte encrypted payload) — classic C2 check-in/tasking behavior |

Unrelated benign traffic also noted for completeness: a legitimate Adobe Acrobat update check to `acroipm2.adobe.com` (`ProcessMAU.txt`, response body `true`) — not part of the malicious chain.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` (HTTP) — payload staging (`/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`) and ongoing beacon C2 (`/`). No DNS resolution preceded contact — the IP is hardcoded in the malware.

**Malicious/phishing domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — resolves to `104.21.55.70`, `172.67.170.159` (Cloudflare-fronted phishing page)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — same infrastructure/domain family, also contacted over HTTPS (TLS SNI)

**Malicious URL**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — served the malicious ZIP
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — DLL payload retrieval

**Transferred files**
| File name | Size | Type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside the ZIP served by checkfedexexp.com) | 6,990,020 bytes | JScript, junk-padded/obfuscated | not separately hashed (delivered inside the ZIP object above) |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | 159,232 bytes | PE32+ DLL (x86-64) | **b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6** |

**Notable supporting artifacts**
- Beacon User-Agent: `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`
- DLL debug path: `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`
- Ad/redirect-chain domains seen adjacent to the lure (possible malvertising/TDS involvement): `nelreports.net`, `exp-tas.com`, `scorecardresearch.com`

## 5. Recommended action
Isolate 10.8.15.133 from the network immediately, reset the `plucero` domain credentials (Kerberos tickets were actively issued to this account during the infection window), and block/hunt for `72.5.43.29` and `*.checkfedexexp.com` across the environment.
